description: Somos NuVaryth, un equipo multidisciplinario interesado en la ingeniería, la tecnología y la exploración espacial. Reunimos conocimientos en mecatrónica, programación, electrónica, diseño 3D y planificación. Queremos desarrollar un juego interactivo para diseñar y simular misiones espaciales mediante decisiones basadas en datos y principios científicos. Buscamos participantes con interés en videojuegos, modelado 3D, física, astronomía y comunicación científica.
summary: Nuvaryth is a mission design game for the "Space Mission Design Game" challenge. Players step into mission control, design a spacecraft where every part costs power, mass and data, fly it through real orbital geometry, and bring the data home to a ground station in Lima, Peru. Each mission starts with a science question and ends with results delivered to the player. Decisions have visible consequences: a wrong choice can mean a lost mission. Nuvaryth Studio, an early prototype, lets players model their own spacecraft parts. The goal is to teach how engineers trade off limited resources in real missions, using NASA data and models.
details:
Nuvaryth is a Unity game that connects the design, management and simulation of a space mission. Players work in a first-person mission control room, configure a satellite, launch it and fly it around Earth. A ground station in Lima, Peru tracks each pass: the antenna follows the satellite in azimuth and elevation, the link only opens above a 5-degree elevation mask, and the player sees how many megabytes were actually delivered. Power, mass and data budgets create real trade-offs, and the end-of-mission report shows the consequences of each choice. Luna 01 (a Moon mission) is shown as in development. Nuvaryth Studio is a prototype tool for modeling spacecraft parts.

How it works: built in Unity with a physical-units model of orbital geometry, solar illumination, topocentric contact with the ground station, and battery and data budgets. Visuals use real NASA imagery and catalogs (Earth, relief, clouds, night lights, stars, planets). Scenario hardware figures and costs are educational parameters, not NASA measurements. A React and TypeScript website presents the missions, the demo video and the credits.

Benefits: players learn systems-engineering thinking, because every subsystem competes for limited resources and a mission is judged by the science it returns. What we hope to achieve: a playable educational tool for students and the public, expanded with the Luna 01 mission and community-built spacecraft in Studio.

Tools: Unity 6, C#, UI Toolkit, HLSL shaders; React, TypeScript, Vite and Netlify for the website; ffmpeg for the demo video; Python scripts for NASA data layers.

AI disclosure: code was assisted by OpenAI Codex and Claude Code (Anthropic). The demo voiceover is AI-generated (Higgsfield Seed Audio 1.0, voice Emmett) and declared in the video metadata and on the website. The demo picture is a real screen recording of the game. The game's opening cinematic is AI-generated (Higgsfield Seedance) and labeled on screen. No generated content uses NASA logos or mission identifiers. Details: https://nuvaryth.study
